01 Biography

Professor Shuzhi Sam Ge received his Ph.D. and DIC from Imperial College London, U.K., in January and July 1993 respectively, and his B.Sc. degree from the Beijing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Beijing, China, in 1986. Before joining NUS, he worked as post-doctoral research associate at Leicester University, UK, from May 1992 - June 1993.

He has been with the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, the National University of Singapore (NUS), since 1993. He first joined as a Lecturer and was promoted through the ranks of Senior Lecturer in 1998, Associate Professor in 2000 to Full Professorship in 2005. At NUS, he has held various leadership roles including (i) Member of Senate Delegate, National University of Singapore, 2008-2010, (ii) Senior Faculty Fellow, NUS Graduate School (NGS) Integrative Sciences and Engineering Programme (ISEP), 2003-Present, (iii) the founding Director of Social Robotics Lab, Interactive Digital Media Institute (IDMI), 2007-2021, (iv) PI member of the Keppel-NUS Corporate Lab, 2014-2018, and National Technology Centre for Offshore and Marine, Singapore (TCOMS), 2018-present, and (v) PI Member of NUS Guangzhou Research Translation and Innovation Institute (GRTII), June 2025-present.

His work has been recognized at the national level in Singapore. Under the National Aerospace Technology Program, aimed at enhancing the competitiveness of local aerospace companies, our team successfully completed a SMART 3D polishing/blending Robotic System on 31 August 1998. The team from NUS, SIMTech and the local company, Turbine Overhaul Services Pte Ltd, was awarded the National Technology Award (currently President’s Technology Award) by the National Science & Technology Board, Singapore in 1999.

He serves/served as (i) President, 2024-2026, President Elect, 2022-2024, Asian Control Association; (ii) IFAC executive officers as a Council Member, 2023-2026, (iii) IEEE Roger W. Brockett Control Systems Award Committee, 2024-2026; Vice President for Technical Activities (2009-2010), Vice President of Membership Activities (2011-2012), and Member of the Board of Governors, of IEEE Control Systems Society, (iv) Chair of International Standing Committee, International Conference on Social Robotics, 2010-present.

He is passionate about engaging a wider audience in research and education, and (i) founded and served as the Editor-in-Chief, http://www.springer.com/engineering/journal/10846 (IJSR), Springer Nature, 2008-2021 and as the Founding Editor-in-Chief, IJSR, 2021-present, and (ii) served/serves as either a Senior Editor or an Associate Editor for a number of flagship journals including IEEE Transaction on SMC-Systems, IEEE Transactions on Automatic Control, IEEE Transactions on Control Systems Technology, IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks, and Automatica, CAAI Transactions on Intelligence Technology, and (iv) serves as Book Editor of the Taylor & Francis Automation and Control Engineering Series.

He is a Fellow of Singapore Academy of Engineering (SAEng), International Academy of Artificial Intelligence Sciences (AAIS), IEEE, IFAC, IET, CCA, ACA and AIIA. Ge is a (co-)author of 10 books, edited 13 books and over 800 international journal and conference papers with a Google Scholar h-index of 126 and more than 70,000 citations (as of March 2026). He has been a Clarivate Highly Cited Researcher consecutively 2016-2025, and ranked 47 in the world and 4 in Singapore, 2026 Research.com Electronics and Electrical Engineering.

His current research interests evolve around Stable Artificial Intelligence (AI), Embodied AI, Intelligent Control, Human Robot Interaction, Societal Robotics, and Research Translation. He has successfully secured over 36.0 million in recent 5 years and over 46.9 million since 1996 in Singapore, plus EU 2.5 million with colleagues as PI, Co-PI and Team PI.

02 Research

Professor Ge’s research spans the entire spectrum of intelligent systems, from mathematical modelling, perception and learning through intelligent control to real-world deployment. His work forms one continuous arc: rigorous theory for adaptive, neural and nonlinear control — including Barrier Lyapunov functions, switched systems and stable learning — provides the guarantees; perception and machine learning give machines an understanding of uncertain and changing worlds; and intelligent control closes the loop with stability, safety and robustness, carrying algorithms all the way onto physical machines operating among people. Across embodied and social robotics, autonomous vehicles, agile mobile and aerial robots, offshore and marine systems and precision manufacturing, modelling, perception, control and deployment are treated not as separate disciplines but as one integrated pipeline. Supported by more than S$46 million in competitive research funding since 1996, his programmes have delivered autonomous urban robots, unmanned vehicles and social robots, robotic turbine-blade finishing and intelligent offshore platforms — systems grounded in theory, validated on real machines and translated into value for industry and society.

03 Grants

As (Co-)Principal Investigator, Professor Ge has led 20+ funded programmes and platforms in embodied AI, robotics and autonomous systems. His funding totals over S$36.0 million in the last five years and S$46.9 million since 1996.

Development of Stable, Robust and Secure Intelligent Systems for Autonomous Vehicles ↗

Principal Investigator · AI Singapore Grand Challenge Award in Robust AI · 2023–2026

Ge leads this award-winning programme on dependable perception and control for autonomous vehicles facing unfamiliar conditions or adversarial interference. It develops multimodal defence using complementary camera and LiDAR information, unified spatio-temporal refinement and stable learning-based control, validated through digital-twin simulation and physical trials.

MR2 — Modular Reconfigurable Mobile Robots

Team Principal Investigator · A*STAR · 2025–2028

MR2 develops modular mobile robots whose chassis, drive, navigation and payload modules can be interchanged to fit different tasks, supporting customisation, repair, upgrade and reuse. As Team PI, Ge addresses configuration-aware modelling, intelligent trajectory tracking and control allocation when a robot’s mechanical configuration changes, extending adaptive intelligent control to flexible, reconfigurable platforms.

INPACE: INdo-PACific-European Hub for Digital Partnerships ↗

Singapore Lead and Asian Co-lead · Horizon Europe · 2024–2027

Ge is Singapore Lead and Asian Co-lead of INPACE, a Horizon Europe hub connecting Europe and the Indo-Pacific on trustworthy digital technologies — artificial intelligence, future chips and networks — across Singapore, Japan, Korea and India. He chaired the EU–Indo-Pacific Digital Partnership Conference 2025 in Singapore, linking technical research with sustained international collaboration.

Social Robots: Breathing Life Into Machines

Principal Investigator · MDA / National Research Foundation · 2007–2012

As PI of this flagship programme, Ge developed socially aware robots that communicate with people and participate in human environments — from companions for the elderly to medical and assistive robots. The programme connected intention estimation, affective interaction and cooperative behaviour, and helped build the field through the International Journal of Social Robotics and the ICSR conference series.

Meta-Learning of Robust State Estimation for Agile Mobile Robots

Co-Principal Investigator · MoE Tier 2 AcRF · 2025–2028

Develops meta-learning methods that let agile mobile robots estimate their own state robustly and adapt quickly to new platforms, sensors and operating conditions from limited data. Learned motion priors are combined with model-based estimation for reliable localisation of fast ground robots in uncertain environments.

Meta-Learning for Fast-Adaptive Control of Aerial Robotic Systems

Co-Principal Investigator · MoE Tier 2 AcRF · 2024–2026

Develops meta-learning control that allows aerial robots to adapt rapidly in flight to changing payloads, dynamics and disturbances. Learned priors are combined with guaranteed nonlinear control, aiming at fast, stable adaptation of quadrotors across tasks without lengthy retraining.

ENFORCE — Enabling Future Systems for Offshore Wind Resources

Co-Investigator · A*STAR · 2023–2027

A large national programme enabling future offshore wind energy systems, including the design and validation of floating offshore wind platforms — such as semi-submersible concepts developed with TCOMS and industry. Ge contributes intelligent modelling, sensing and control of offshore structures and operations within the multi-institution programme.

Coupled Engine–Vessel Physics with Data-Driven AI Models for Carbon Emissions Estimation

Co-Principal Investigator · Singapore Maritime Institute · 2023–2025

Develops coupled physics-informed and data-driven AI models of ship engines and vessel behaviour to estimate carbon emissions accurately under real operating conditions, supporting maritime decarbonisation with trustworthy emissions monitoring for vessels at sea.

Material Robotics Laboratory (MRL)

Principal Investigator · Institute for Functional Intelligent Materials, MOE · 2022–2023

The Material Robotics Laboratory explores robots whose sensing, actuation and intelligence arise from functional materials themselves — soft, active and multifunctional matter. The programme links materials science with robotics and control, laying groundwork for compliant, adaptive and bio-inspired machines.

ENSURE — Enhancing Offshore System Productivity, Integrity and Survivability in Extreme Environments

Principal Investigator · A*STAR · 2020–2023

ENSURE enhances the productivity, structural integrity and survivability of offshore assets in extreme environments through smart sensing, modelling and digital twins, with real-time predictive frameworks for fatigue and structural response that support safer decisions and de-manning under intensifying storm conditions.

Robust Adaptive Learning Control of a Floatel against Certain/Uncertain Shielding Effects

Principal Investigator · National Research Foundation · 2014–2018

Develops robust adaptive learning control for semi-submersible floatels operating alongside FPSOs, where shielding effects from the nearby vessel strongly disturb waves and motions. The research aims to maintain safe, smooth gangway operations and extend operational uptime, while informing the design of next-generation floatels for deep-water operations.

Distributed Sensing and Perception

Principal Investigator · A*STAR SERC · 2013–2015

Develops distributed sensing and perception for robotic welding and finishing in automated factories: complementary sensors distributed across the workspace are fused for high-resolution 3D reconstruction, inspection, process monitoring and safety, enabling robots to perceive and adapt across pre-, in- and post-process stages.

URBAN-NAV — Urban Outdoor Navigation of Unmanned Platforms under GPS-Challenged Environments

Co-Principal Investigator · Defence Innovative Research Programme · 2013–2015

Tackles navigation of unmanned platforms in GPS-denied urban canyons by fusing panoramic vision, visual odometry and inertial sensing with road-model constraints and Monte-Carlo localisation, maintaining accurate vehicle positioning in dense cities without reliance on GPS satellites.

Robotics for Autism Assessment

Principal Investigator · 2012–2015

Investigates social robots as standardised, engaging instruments for early autism assessment. A humanoid robot elicits social cues from young children during semi-structured play with clinicians, while automated video and behaviour analysis supports earlier, more objective characterisation of social responsiveness.

Mind Robotics

Principal Investigator · NUS Tier 1 · 2008–2011

Mind Robotics develops brain–robot interfaces that analyse features extracted from EEG signals to communicate with and control robots. The project built a prototype two-channel wireless EEG acquisition system with novel active electrodes, linking neural signals directly to robotic action.

Modelling and Control of Subsea Installation Operations

Principal Investigator · Lloyd’s Register Professorship Fund · 2007–2011

Develops modelling and control methods for subsea installation operations, addressing the dynamics of lowering and placing subsea hardware through the water column and onto the seabed for safer, more precise offshore installation.

Intelligent Deepwater Mooring Systems

Principal Investigator · A*STAR–MPA Joint Grant / CORE · 2007–2011

Develops intelligent modelling and control for deepwater mooring systems under the Offshore Technology Research Programme, addressing station-keeping and mooring dynamics of floating assets in deep water to improve the safety and operability of offshore mooring operations.

Development of a Fully Autonomous Mobile Urban Robot for the TechX Challenge

Principal Investigator · NUS (with I²R) · 2007–2011

Led Team X-1, a joint NUS–I²R team, in developing the X1 fully autonomous mobile urban robot for the DSTA TechX Challenge. The robot navigated unknown outdoor and indoor urban environments — including stairs and obstacles — and located targets without human intervention, advancing autonomous navigation, perception and mission planning.

Advanced Intelligent Control for Hard Disk Drives in Mobile Applications

Principal Investigator · SERC A*STAR, with DSI and UT Arlington · 2006–2009

Developed advanced intelligent control for hard disk drives in mobile applications in collaboration with the Data Storage Institute and the University of Texas at Arlington, addressing high-precision servo tracking under vibration and motion disturbances and extending adaptive nonlinear control to precision mechatronics.

Integrative Serviceability Management and Supervisory Control of Networked Manufacturing Systems for Virtual Enterprises

Co-Principal Investigator · A*STAR SERC TSRP (DRAM) · 2006–2009

Developed integrative serviceability management and supervisory control with dynamic resource allocation for networked manufacturing, connecting distributed factories through networked supervision to support responsive manufacturing across enterprise boundaries.

Intelligent Control of Unmanned Vehicles

Principal Investigator · Defence Science & Technology Agency (DSTA) · 2002–2005

Developed intelligent control of unmanned vehicles, applying adaptive and neural control to uncertain vehicle dynamics for precise navigation and tracking in field conditions. The programme underpinned the inaugural Temasek Young Investigator Award on Intelligent Control of Unmanned Vehicles.

Interactive Robotic Usher

Co-Principal Investigator · in collaboration with I²R · 2001–2003

Built a prototype humanoid service robot for guest reception, integrating visual human–robot interaction to guide and assist visitors — an early step toward intelligent service robots that support people in daily environments.

Automated 3D Blending System for Turbine Blades and Vanes

Co-Principal Investigator · NSTB & Turbine Overhaul Services · 1996–1998

Co-developed an automated robotic 3D blending (polishing) system for turbine blades and vanes with Turbine Overhaul Services. The SMART 3D polishing/blending robotic system won the Singapore National Technology Award in 1999 — an early end-to-end translation of intelligent robotics into industrial deployment.

04 Selected Publications

2009— citations
Constrained control

Barrier Lyapunov functions for the control of output-constrained nonlinear systems ↗

Tee, K. P., Ge, S. S., & Tay, E. H.

Automatica, 45(4), 918–927.

Pioneered the use of Barrier Lyapunov Functions for output-constrained nonlinear control, embedding constraint enforcement directly in the stability analysis. By making the Lyapunov function grow unbounded as the output approaches a prescribed boundary, the design links bounded closed-loop behaviour to satisfaction of the output constraint under the paper’s assumptions. This work gives a constructive mathematical route from conventional tracking control to control with explicit safety limits, and provides a foundation for subsequent research on constrained intelligent systems.

2005— citations
Switched systems

Switched linear systems: control and design ↗

Sun, Z., & Ge, S. S.

Springer London.

Established a systematic treatment of switched linear systems, bringing controllability, observability, stability and control design into a common framework. The monograph develops geometric and algebraic characterizations that reveal how switching changes what a system can achieve, together with methods for designing switching laws and feedback controllers. Its contribution is to make the interaction between continuous dynamics and discrete switching amenable to verifiable analysis, providing a theoretical basis for the design of hybrid control systems.

2013— citations
Stable neural control

Stable adaptive neural network control ↗

Ge, S. S., Hang, C. C., Lee, T. H., & Zhang, T.

Springer Science & Business Media. 2013 eBook.

Developed a systematic foundation for stable adaptive neural-network control of uncertain nonlinear systems. The monograph connects the approximation capabilities of neural networks with Lyapunov-based controller design, so that adaptation is analysed as part of the closed-loop dynamics. It addresses the central challenge of obtaining useful learning behaviour while establishing stability and tracking properties. This framework helped make neural control a mathematically grounded approach to systems whose nonlinear dynamics cannot be modelled precisely in advance.

2011— citations
Input constraints

Adaptive tracking control of uncertain MIMO nonlinear systems with input constraints ↗

Chen, M., Ge, S. S., & Ren, B.

Automatica, 47(3), 452–465.

Extended adaptive tracking control to uncertain multi-input multi-output nonlinear systems with constrained actuator inputs. The design explicitly accounts for input saturation through an auxiliary system, integrating the actuator limitation into the adaptive-control analysis. This addresses a practical gap between unconstrained control laws and the finite authority of physical actuators. The result links tracking performance, uncertainty compensation and input constraints within one design framework, with boundedness properties established under the assumptions stated in the paper.

2004— citations
MIMO nonlinear control

Adaptive neural control of uncertain MIMO nonlinear systems ↗

Ge, S. S., & Wang, C.

IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks, 15(3), 674–692.

Developed adaptive neural control for coupled, uncertain multi-input multi-output nonlinear systems. By exploiting the system’s block-triangular structure, the work constructs controllers for classes of systems in which nonlinear coupling makes direct inversion difficult. Neural approximation is combined with stability analysis to establish semiglobal uniform ultimate boundedness while avoiding controller singularities for the considered classes. It advances the broader programme of extending intelligent adaptive control from simpler single-channel models to interacting nonlinear systems.

2000— citations
Adaptive backstepping

Adaptive neural network control for strict-feedback nonlinear systems using backstepping design ↗

Zhang, T., Ge, S. S., & Hang, C. C.

Automatica, 36(12), 1835–1846.

Combined neural-network approximation with recursive backstepping design for uncertain strict-feedback nonlinear systems. At successive stages of the design, neural models compensate for unknown nonlinear functions while a Lyapunov argument links the stages into a closed-loop stability analysis. The paper provides a constructive method for developing adaptive controllers when an accurate plant model is unavailable. It forms part of the theoretical foundation for later work on learning-based nonlinear control, including efforts to manage the complexity of recursive controller design.

1998— citations
Robot control

Adaptive neural network control of robotic manipulators ↗

Ge, S. S., Lee, T. H., & Harris, C. J.

World Scientific.

Connected the physical structure of robotic manipulators with adaptive neural-network control. The monograph brings robot dynamics, neural approximation and Lyapunov-based analysis together to address control in the presence of uncertain nonlinear dynamics. Its significance lies in treating learning and mechanical-system stability as parts of the same control problem, rather than assessing approximation quality alone. This provides a theoretical foundation for intelligent robot control that retains an explicit connection to the structure and behaviour of the physical machine.

2010— citations
Robust neural control

Robust adaptive neural network control for a class of uncertain MIMO nonlinear systems with input nonlinearities ↗

Chen, M., Ge, S. S., & How, B. V. E.

IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks, 21(5), 796–812.

Addressed uncertain multi-input multi-output nonlinear systems in which the actuator input itself is nonlinear. The paper combines robust adaptive design with neural-network approximation to compensate for uncertainty while analysing the stability of the resulting closed loop. By treating input nonlinearities within the control problem, it extends the applicability of adaptive neural control beyond ideal actuator models. This contributes to the development of intelligent controllers that account for both uncertain plant dynamics and non-ideal actuation under stated modelling assumptions.

2011— citations
Switched-system stability

Stability theory of switched dynamical systems ↗

Sun, Z., & Ge, S. S.

Springer London.

Developed a unified account of stability analysis for switched dynamical systems, examining how the dynamics of individual subsystems interact with the switching signal. The monograph distinguishes stability under different switching conditions and relates analytical criteria to the design of stabilizing switching strategies. Its importance is in showing why subsystem-level properties alone do not settle the stability of the combined system, and in providing systematic tools for reasoning about hybrid dynamics and constructing switching laws with verifiable stability properties.

08 Courses

Teaching at the National University of Singapore spans the full stack of intelligent robotics — machine learning, human–robot interaction and autonomous robot systems — combining rigorous theory with extensive hands-on implementation.

EE4705, EE5112

Human–Robot Interaction

Fundamental concepts, modes and algorithms of physical and non-physical human–robot interaction — from human detection, behaviour and intention understanding to human-aware motion planning for collaborative, assistive and wearable robots.

View on NUSMods ↗
CEG5301

Machine Learning with Applications

A comprehensive introduction to machine learning and deep learning, covering supervised, unsupervised and reinforcement learning and neural network architectures, with hands-on projects in healthcare, computer vision, natural language processing, robotics and cybersecurity.

View on NUSMods ↗
CEG5303

Autonomous Robot Systems

Concepts and methods that make mobile ground robots and unmanned aerial vehicles autonomous — path planning, sensor fusion, obstacle avoidance and mapping — implemented in simulation and on robots through the Robot Operating System (ROS).

View on NUSMods ↗
